The test image shows a mango leaf with multiple small, dark brown to black spots scattered across the leaf surface. The spots are irregular in shape, some with slightly sunken or necrotic centers. The leaf is still mostly green. No white powdery coating, no sooty black layer, no tip dieback.

This pattern — discrete dark lesions scattered across a green leaf — is classic Anthracnose. Now let me confirm with one reference image.

The Anthracnose reference shows a heavily damaged, yellowed leaf — more advanced stage. However, the test image shows early-stage discrete dark spots on a green leaf, which is still consistent with Anthracnose (early infection produces scattered dark lesions before leaf yellowing). Powdery Mildew would show white powder, Sooty Mould a black coating, and Die Back affects stem tips — none match the scattered spot pattern seen here.
